source_metadata.question:
A circle with radius $1$ is inscribed in a square and circumscribed about another square as shown. Which fraction is closest to the ratio of the circle's shaded area to the area between the two squares?

<image1>
source_metadata.subject: metric geometry - area

target.visual_information: A shaded region with an adjacent unshaded interior cutout or excluded part. On the left, use the light-blue patch inside the large semicircle and above both smaller arcs. On the right, use the shaded parts inside the circle and outside the central white diamond.
target.left_evidence: The light-blue patch inside the large semicircle and above both smaller arcs.
target.right_evidence: The shaded parts inside the circle and outside the central white diamond.
target.left_meaning: It comprises the large semicircle minus the two unshaded smaller semicircles.
target.right_meaning: The selected circular part is the disk with the inner square excluded. The additional corner shading is outside the circle.
target.reason: The shade identifies the remainder after leaving designated pieces out of an enclosing geometric area. Those pieces must be removed from the area computation in each panel.
target.reasoning_consequence: Correctly interpreting the markings means subtracting both smaller semicircle areas from the outer semicircle area on the left and using the diamond as an exclusion and omitting the shaded outer corners when calculating the circular area fraction on the right.
